A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GleSAM/LQSeg work. The supplied text, equations, tables, figures, and supplemental material are readable. The original sections and experiments can be matched reliably against v3's expanded content.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation experiments on ThinObject-5K, LVIS, ECSSD, and COCO, together with component ablations and sensitivity analyses in Tables 1–9.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds BDD-100K evaluation, backbone comparisons, prompt experiments, and qualitative results in Sections 7–10.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same single-step latent denoising, FDA scaling, CRE weight replication, LoRA adaptation, and two-stage training with unchanged losses. Algorithms 1–2 document the existing procedure; the additional backbone evaluations do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: V3 adds evaluation on real driving imagery from BDD-100K, extending coverage beyond the synthetic degradation benchmarks in v1. It also evaluates ground-truth and perturbed bounding-box prompts, broadening input conditions beyond the earlier point-prompt experiments. The original training and evaluation datasets remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the original comparisons remains unchanged: SAM, SAM2, RobustSAM, and the PromptIR/DiffBIR restoration pipelines. Added experiments use existing comparator families. The ViT and Hiera variants are model configurations, while newly cited DN-DETR supplies a box-noise convention rather than an evaluated segmentation baseline.

E3.justification: Sections 7.2–7.4 add systematic evaluations across ViT-B/L/H and Hiera-T/S/B/L, point counts from 1 to 10, and ground-truth versus noisy boxes with noise scale 0.2. The original three-click default, metrics, optimizer, batch size, and training budgets remain unchanged. These are substantial additional protocols.

E4.justification: V3 retains the original component, decoder, channel-expansion, gamma, LoRA-rank, and degradation-level analyses. It adds backbone and prompt sensitivity studies in Tables 11–13 and Figure 8, further feature-reconstruction comparisons, and extensive qualitative cases under unseen degradations and on COCO. These broaden the evidence about robustness and generalization.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, performance error bars, or significance tests. The added tables and curves continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice. Noise standard deviations in v3 describe degradation generation, not uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain their numerical results. New Table 10 reports BDD-100K IoU of 0.8775 for GleSAM versus 0.8650 for SAM, and 0.9087 for GleSAM2 versus 0.8891 for SAM2. Tables 11–13 and Figure 8 add backbone and prompt results; Figure 8 includes a one-point case where GleSAM2 trails SAM2. These are additional evaluations, not improved scores for the original experiments.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, reconstruction objective, segmentation objective, and underlying assumptions are retained. New Equation 7 expresses the already described blur/resize/noise/JPEG degradation composition symbolically. It adds no substantive mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: generative latent enhancement for SAM/SAM2, FDA and CRE, LQSeg, and robustness across degraded, clear, and unseen-degradation images. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: Section 7.3 newly attributes noisy-box robustness to enhanced latent representations reducing noise-induced ambiguity. Section 7.4 connects increasing point counts with reduced prompt ambiguity and performance gains. These extend the interpretation to prompt conditions, although Figure 8 does not support the accompanying claim of superiority at every point count. No substantive limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: Sections 8–9 add degradation-generation settings, including kernel choices, parameter ranges, noise probabilities, and JPEG quality factors. They also disclose T=1000, prompt-generation procedures, and training/inference pseudocode. The abstract adds a code/dataset release link. These substantially fill documentation gaps; they do not establish changes to the previously used method or data-generation procedure.

R1.justification: V3 adds eight supporting references, including ViT, Hiera, BDD-100K, DN-DETR, and corruption or degradation-generation research. The related-work discussion and positioning against robust segmentation and diffusion-based perception remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The retained abstract, introduction, method, experimental discussion, and conclusion are largely unchanged in wording and organization. Sections 7–10 organize the additional experiments and documentation, alongside affiliation, release, and acknowledgement additions. There is limited rewriting of the original narrative.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 10–13, Figures 8–15, and Algorithms 1–2, including prompt-count plots, backbone comparisons, feature maps, and several full-page qualitative displays. Figure 3 is simplified by removing displayed loss branches. These constitute substantial visual additions beyond the accompanying text reflow.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens validation and reproducibility: BDD-100K addresses v1's reliance on synthetic degradation evaluations, the backbone and prompt studies test broader applicability, and Sections 8–9 supply important missing construction and implementation details. New reporting problems qualify these gains: Figure 8 contradicts blanket prompt-superiority wording, and Table 12's GleSAM2-L average pixel accuracy exceeds every contributing score. These localized issues do not outweigh the substantial improvements to the evidence and documentation supporting the central contributions.
